_notes: Non-rendered field: destination facts and seasonality findings only. The app ignores keys it does not know. Planning rationale and open questions are kept outside the repo.

LANDSCAPE MIX: this route deliberately spans two opposite landscapes — Colorado's green high country (aspen, spruce, alpine lakes, 3,000 m passes) and Utah's red-rock desert. It is weighted toward Colorado: 9 of 20 nights in the mountains against 6 in Utah, only two Utah bases (Moab for Arches and Canyonlands, Springdale for Zion — a green river canyon rather than open desert). The full Utah 'Mighty 5' circuit is deliberately NOT attempted; Capitol Reef and Bryce are drive-through stops on the transfer day, not bases.

SEASONALITY — COLORADO FALL COLOUR (verified Aug 2026; re-checked 30 Aug 2026): peak is EARLY, and this is the real tension. Forecast 2026 peaks are 18-30 September for the Collegiate Peaks, Aspen, Leadville and Crested Butte, and 27 September - 5 October for Telluride and the rest of the San Juans. An early-October start catches the tail of San Juan colour; the Aspen area will already be past peak. A trip starting in mid-October misses the aspens entirely.

SEASONALITY — PASSES: Independence Pass (CO 82, Aspen to Twin Lakes) typically closes for winter in late October to mid-November — it closed 17 Nov in 2025 — but the first big storm can shut it early. October is normally fine; have the alternative via I-70 and Glenwood Springs in your pocket. Trail Ridge Road in Rocky Mountain NP closes to through travel mid-to-late October (25 Oct in 2024); an early-October visit is safe, later is not.

SEASONALITY — NEVADA: Great Basin NP was considered and dropped. The Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive is only open roughly June-October and closes on snow, and the park is a long detour from anything else. Las Vegas is used purely as a flight bookend instead.
SEASONALITY — UTAH: no problem. October is the best month — 10-27°C, thin crowds, and Arches has no timed-entry requirement in 2026. Zion still runs its shuttle in the main canyon.
ROUTING: open-jaw, Denver (DEN) in and Las Vegas (LAS) out. A loop back to Denver would add two full driving days for nothing.
DRIVING NOTE: every leg is inside the 4-6h cap except Moab to Springdale, which is about 5h30 and is deliberately broken with a stop at Capitol Reef. That is the one long day of the trip.

title: Aspens to Red Rock: A Three-Week Western US Road Trip

ideaImage.caption: Aspen turning in the Colorado high country

brief: Three weeks of big American driving, front-loaded with the green stuff. Ten nights in Colorado's high country — aspen gold, alpine passes, mining towns and the Million Dollar Highway — then south into red rock for arches, slot canyons and Zion, finishing at Las Vegas for the flight home. Enormous scenery, great roads, and burgers the whole way.
vibe: Aspen gold to red rock canyons

facts.flexibleRangeDays: 20-22 — Salt Lake City is the optional night
facts.bestSeason: Late September–early October — the only window that catches Colorado's aspens before the passes close
facts.timezone: Mountain Time; Arizona skips daylight saving, so it runs an hour behind Utah in October
facts.driving: Right-hand traffic, superb roads, long distances, high-altitude passes

itinerary.description: Land in the evening and sleep near the airport at a comfortable 1,600 m.
A day or two in the city before going up — brewpubs, a huge bookshop, and Red Rocks in the foothills.
Straight into the high country — alpine lakes, elk in rut, and Trail Ridge Road over 3,700 m while it is still open.
Over Independence Pass, then the Maroon Bells, a ghost town up the valley, and a gondola over turning aspen.
The Million Dollar Highway, hot springs in the middle of town, and a steam train out of Silverton.
The longest drive of the trip, broken at the Mesa Verde cliff dwellings, then slot canyons and Horseshoe Bend.
North through Monument Valley to sandstone arches, a mesa-top canyon rim, and a very different kind of enormous.
A night between the red rock and Zion — Temple Square, the Great Salt Lake, and a proper city to restock in.
A green river canyon with 600 m walls, cottonwoods turning yellow, and a shuttle that does the driving.
Two and a half hours down, and one full night of neon, buffets and outlet malls.
A morning loop of Red Rock Canyon, then fly home.

primaryHighlights.title: Colorado's High Country
primaryHighlights.description: Aspen gold, alpine lakes and road passes above 3,500 m, with old mining towns and hot springs at the bottom of them.
primaryHighlights.caption: Aspen town below the ski runs

primaryHighlights.title: The Million Dollar Highway
primaryHighlights.description: Cliff-edge switchbacks with no guardrail, climbing over three high passes. The drive of the trip.
primaryHighlights.caption: Highway ledge cut into rock

primaryHighlights.title: The Red Rock Country
primaryHighlights.description: A total change of landscape for the last week — arches, mesas, slot canyons, and rock that glows at either end of the day.
primaryHighlights.caption: Delicate Arch from the viewpoint trail

natureHighlights.title: Trail Ridge Road, Rocky Mountain NP
natureHighlights.description: The highest continuous paved road in the US, running above the treeline for 18 km with nothing but tundra either side.
natureHighlights.caption: Trail Ridge Road above the treeline

natureHighlights.title: Maroon Bells
natureHighlights.description: The most photographed mountains in North America, over a lake ringed with aspen. An easy 6 km loop around the shoreline.
natureHighlights.caption: Maroon Bells reflected in Maroon Lake

natureHighlights.title: Canyonlands & Mesa Arch
natureHighlights.description: A mesa top with 600 m drops on three sides, and short rim walks to viewpoints that go on forever.
natureHighlights.caption: Mesa Arch glowing at sunrise

natureHighlights.title: Zion Canyon
natureHighlights.description: The greenest place in Utah — a river, cottonwoods and 600 m sandstone walls closing in overhead.
natureHighlights.caption: Overlook down into Zion Canyon

natureHighlights.title: Monument Valley
natureHighlights.description: Sandstone buttes standing 300 m out of flat red desert, on the drive between Page and Moab.
natureHighlights.caption: Horseback rider at John Ford's Point

natureHighlights.title: Bryce Canyon
natureHighlights.description: Thousands of orange rock spires standing in a natural amphitheatre, seen from a rim walk on the drive south.
natureHighlights.caption: The Bryce Amphitheater hoodoos

cityHighlights.title: Estes Park
cityHighlights.description: A cheerful gateway town of taffy shops and outfitters, right at the park entrance.
cityHighlights.caption: Elkhorn Avenue shopfronts in autumn

cityHighlights.title: Ouray
cityHighlights.description: “The Switzerland of America” — a Victorian mining town wedged into a box canyon barely wide enough to hold it.
cityHighlights.caption: Main Street, downtown Ouray

cityHighlights.title: Las Vegas
cityHighlights.description: Neon, enormous hotels and outlet malls — pure spectacle after three weeks of mountains and rock.
cityHighlights.caption: The Strip lit up at night

cityHighlights.title: Denver
cityHighlights.description: A mile-high city with a walkable centre, and the right place to spend two nights getting used to the altitude before going higher.
cityHighlights.caption: Downtown Denver skyline from the interstate

cityHighlights.title: Salt Lake City
cityHighlights.description: A wide, flat, mountain-ringed city laid out on a grid, with Temple Square at the middle of it and the Wasatch range straight above.
cityHighlights.caption: Skyline below the Wasatch Range

culinaryHighlights.title: Green Chile Cheeseburgers
culinaryHighlights.description: The Southwest's contribution to the burger — roasted green chile piled on top. Found at roadside shacks all the way down.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Green chile cheeseburger and fries

culinaryHighlights.title: Mountain Town Breakfast
culinaryHighlights.description: Enormous diner breakfasts in Estes Park, Aspen and Ouray — pancakes, hash browns and bottomless coffee before a hike.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Eggs, bacon and pancakes

culinaryHighlights.title: Moab Roadside Barbecue
culinaryHighlights.description: Smoked brisket, ribs and pulled pork from trailers and shacks on the highway into town, sold by weight on butcher paper.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Brisket, ribs and sausage

culinaryHighlights.title: American Fast Food
culinaryHighlights.description: The real thing, done properly and everywhere from Utah onward — In-N-Out, Whataburger, Chick-fil-A, and a drive-through on every corner.
culinaryHighlights.caption: In-N-Out Burger at sunset

culinaryHighlights.title: Mexican Food
culinaryHighlights.description: Real mexican food with desert influences, from tacos and burritos to home-style stuffed poblano and rice platters
culinaryHighlights.caption: Red Iguana in SLC

culinaryHighlights.title: Vegas Dumplings & Noodles
culinaryHighlights.description: Las Vegas quietly has some of the best Asian food in the country — Din Tai Fung on the Strip, and a whole Chinatown of noodle and hotpot places two miles west.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Din Tai Fung, Las Vegas

thingsToDo.title: The Durango & Silverton Steam Railway
thingsToDo.description: A coal-fired narrow-gauge train that has run the Animas river gorge since 1882, on ledges cut into the cliff with no road anywhere near.
thingsToDo.caption: Steam locomotive No. 480

thingsToDo.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
thingsToDo.description: A concert venue wedged between two 90 m sandstone slabs. On non-show days you walk in free, and locals run the steps as a workout.
thingsToDo.caption: Climbing the amphitheatre's stone steps

thingsToDo.title: Antelope Canyon
thingsToDo.description: A slot canyon barely a metre wide in places, with light shafts dropping through from the desert above. Navajo land, so guided only.
thingsToDo.caption: Swirling sandstone walls in the canyon

thingsToDo.title: Horseshoe Bend
thingsToDo.description: A 300 m cliff edge above a near-perfect loop of the Colorado river, fifteen minutes' walk from the car park.
thingsToDo.caption: The Colorado River's horseshoe bend

thingsToDo.title: Ouray Hot Springs
thingsToDo.description: A row of open-air mineral pools at different temperatures, right in the middle of town under the peaks, open year-round.
thingsToDo.caption: Swimmers at the hot springs pool

thingsToDo.title: Red Rock Canyon Scenic Loop
thingsToDo.description: A one-way 21 km loop through red sandstone escarpments half an hour from the Las Vegas Strip — the last thing before the airport.
thingsToDo.caption: Sandstone peaks at dusk

otherPerks: Star fields once you leave the towns — almost no light pollution on the whole route
Three of the great American drives: Trail Ridge, Independence Pass, the Million Dollar Highway
Aspens peak in the San Juans in early October — whole mountainsides turning gold at once
Wildlife without trying: bighorn sheep on the passes, marmots on the trails, elk in the towns
Two nights in Denver first, so the 3,700 m passes never feel like altitude
Big diner breakfasts, green chile on everything, In-N-Out before the flight home
Everything in English, superb roads, and a supermarket in every town
Viewpoints, trailheads and arches are all minutes from wherever you park

primary.heading: Two landscapes, one drive
primary.intro: The trip splits cleanly in half. Ten nights of alpine Colorado — gold aspen, mining towns, passes above the treeline — then the ground turns orange and stays that way through Utah and Arizona to the Nevada border.

nature.heading: Above the treeline, then below the rim
nature.intro: Colorado goes up: alpine lakes, 3,500 m road passes, valleys full of turning aspen. The southwest goes down: arches, mesa edges, slot canyons and a river canyon with 600 m walls.

cities.heading: Mining towns, gateway towns, and one very bright city
cities.intro: A mile-high city to start and acclimatise in, Victorian mining towns wedged into canyons with hot springs at the bottom, a grid-planned city under the Wasatch, and Las Vegas at the very end as a deliberate change of tone.

food.heading: Diners, burgers and roadside barbecue
food.intro: American road food at its best — enormous breakfasts before a hike, green chile on everything, smoked brisket from highway shacks, and a supermarket in every town worth an hour of wandering.

why.heading: What three weeks out here actually buys you
why.intro: Scale, mostly. The drives are the attraction as much as the parks are, and the landscape resets completely halfway through.

thingsToDo.heading: Steam trains, slot canyons and hot springs
thingsToDo.intro: The driving is the spine of this trip. These are the things worth stopping the car for — most of them turn-up-and-go, two of them worth booking the week before.
